{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Emerge seeks to incorporate anti-imperialism in DSA’s labor activism and legislative campaigns.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Rather than enabling the unequal dynamics of world trade to benefit U.S. workers alone, the labor movement should grow militancy and solidarity to oppose oligarchy and colonialism everywhere.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA should advocate for ecosocialist policy built on principles of just global transition and respect for all life, not just for “green growth” for the West.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA’s elected officials should publicly oppose the endless warfare and sanctions the U.S.-led regime exports around the globe.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"To combat capitalism, it is necessary to confront imperialism.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The working class must be actively built and unified through local organizing work, street movements, electoral projects, and coalition building.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"DSA should be a connective tissue of the left ecosystem and a strong collaborator and leader, given its strategic position between movements, labor, and the state.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"DSA should forge broad coalitions and develop new DSA members by organizing at existing and emergent sites of working class struggle.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
